verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: the Court's own PDF on supremecourt.flcourts.gov still could not be stored: on 14, 16 and 17 Oct 2026 the archiver was refused by the robots.txt of the Florida courts' download host. Re-read the copy of the opinion PDF hosted by ALM (assets.alm.com, publisher of Law.com), stored on 14 Oct 2026 and found unchanged on 17 Oct 2026 (Last-Modified 13 Apr 2026), which carries the Court's caption, case number, date, per curiam text, the vote and the appendix with the amended rules; title, date, status, the summary and the notes rest on this third-party copy. Whether the comments have been amended since October 2024 could not be checked against the current Rules Regulating The Florida Bar (floridabar.org refuses automated requests).

title.quote: IN RE: AMENDMENTS TO RULES REGULATING THE FLORIDA BAR – CHAPTER 4.

issuing_body.quote: The Florida Bar has filed a petition proposing amendments to the following portions of Chapter 4 of the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar (rules)
MUÑIZ, C.J., and CANADY, LABARGA, COURIEL, GROSSHANS, FRANCIS, and SASSO, JJ., concur.

date_in_force.quote: The amendments shall become effective October 28, 2024.

status.quote: The amendments shall become effective October 28, 2024.
THE FILING OF A MOTION FOR REHEARING SHALL NOT ALTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THESE AMENDMENTS.

legal_force.quote: Accordingly, we amend the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar as reflected in the appendix to this opinion.

summary.quote: we amend the Comments to rules 4-1.1, 4-1.6, 4-5.1, and 4-5.3, adding a warning about the necessity to take care in using generative artificial intelligence.
including an understanding of the benefits and risks associated with the use of technology, including generative artificial intelligence
For example, a lawyer should be aware that generative artificial intelligence may create risks to the lawyer’s duty of confidentiality.
consider safeguards for the firm’s use of technologies such as generative artificial intelligence
A lawyer should also consider safeguards when assistants use technologies such as generative artificial intelligence.
We also amend rules 4-7.13 and 4-7.15 to allow for testimonials of a celebrity who is a current or former client

notes.quote: except for its proposal to delete references to “zeal” and “zealous” in the Preamble to Chapter 4 and in the comment to rule 4-1.3.

changes.verification.note: rewritten for this recheck; no field of the record changes

judgment.status_reasoning: The Court's opinion of 29 Aug 2024 amends the rules and states that the amendments become effective on 28 Oct 2024, and that a motion for rehearing does not alter that date. Today, 18 Oct 2026, is after that date; no stored file shows a later amendment of the generative-AI comments. 'In force' stands, resting on the third-party copy.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Court-adopted amendments to the binding professional conduct rules for lawyers whose AI content is a set of generative-AI warnings in the comments; borderline and included with the existing scope_note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the opinion's date, 29 Aug 2024; date_in_force is the stated effective date, 28 Oct 2024.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The current summary matches the opinion and its appendix: the four comments (competence, confidentiality, partners' and supervisors' firm policies, nonlawyer assistants and outside services) and the celebrity-testimonial change in rules 4-7.13 and 4-7.15. Left unchanged.

No stored file shows whether the generative-AI comments have been amended since 28 Oct 2024.
